comparison.vsPreBatching: CPU only improved 158% -> 149% (~6%), far short of hoped-for reduction
comparison.vsLegacy: still 3.6x legacy CPU (149% vs 41.7%); RSS still 1.3x lower (2,575KB vs 3,426KB/output)

batchingBottleneckAnalysis: The RESTREAM_EGRESS_VISIT_MAX_US default (2000us = 2ms) is the binding constraint, not visit_max_bytes (256KB, plenty of headroom). But the deeper reason batching barely helped: the fragment-batching change reduces shard wake/poll/schedule overhead per unit, not the NUMBER of srt_send() syscalls, which stays fixed at roughly unit_bytes/1316 regardless of how many happen per scheduler visit. For a 74KB keyframe that is still ~57 separate srt_send() calls; syscall-transition cost appears to dominate, not scheduling overhead. The real next lever is raising SRT's configured message-size ceiling (SRTO_PAYLOADSIZE or equivalent) to shrink the fragment COUNT itself, not just how fragments are scheduled -- this needs dedicated SRT-configuration investigation and is Phase 7 tuning territory, not a quick follow-up.
decodeIntegrity: 171 mediamtx decode-error lines in this churny 100-way ramp (vs 124 pre-batching, vs 3 for legacy) -- run-to-run churn variance, not attributed to a batching regression; srt-crypto-matrix (crypto-fabric17) passed cleanly with correctness spot-checks intact.
decision: EgressRolloutMode default stays Off. Fragment count reduction (larger SRT message size) is required before CPU is competitive enough to reconsider the flip.
